Hi Takashi / Mei — sorry for the confusion, and great question. I confirmed the conversions and the DST situation in Sydney: AEDT is UTC+11 right now which can make some calendar clients show a different date if they default to a different locale. To avoid ambiguity I'm listing each option with explicit local date + time per city below.

Option A (preferred by our SE):
- Tokyo: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 — 10:00 JST (UTC+9)
- Singapore: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 — 09:00 SGT (UTC+8)
- Sydney: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 — 11:00 AEDT (UTC+11)

Option B:
- Tokyo: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 — 15:00 JST (UTC+9)
- Singapore: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 — 14:00 SGT (UTC+8)
- Sydney: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 — 16:00 AEDT (UTC+11)

Option C:
- Tokyo: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 — 09:30 JST (UTC+9)
- Singapore: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 — 08:30 SGT (UTC+8)
- Sydney: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 — 10:30 AEDT (UTC+11)

Action items:
- If Option A works, I'll send a Google Calendar invite that includes all three local times in the description and attach invite.ics for corporate calendars. Monica will create the invite and ensure the event time zones are set explicitly so Outlook/Apple/Google show the same instant across locales.
- Attached again: asia-timezone-guide.png and redwood-demo-agenda.pdf.

Which slot do you prefer? If Mei prefers earlier UTC-aligned times, we can try moving Option A 30 minutes earlier.

Thanks — Marissa
